title: Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.q: Which statement reflects freedom of speech in Australia?
questions.a: People are free to say and write what they think
w: People must not criticise the government

questions.a: People are free to join or not join any organisation
w: People must join a political party

questions.q: In Australia, people are free to follow any religion or no religion. This is called?
What is the Rule of Law?
questions.a: All people including government are bound by law
w: The Prime Minister is above the law

questions.q: What is mateship in Australian context?
questions.a: Helping and receiving help, especially in difficult times

questions.q: In a parliamentary democracy, how do people vote?
In Australia's parliamentary democracy, where does the power of the government come from?
questions.a: The Australian people, who vote for representatives in parliament
questions.e: The power of the government comes from the Australian people, because citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament.

questions.q: Can people in Australia protest against the government?
questions.a: Yes, if the protest is peaceful and within the law
w: Yes, and they can damage property
questions.e: Australians can gather to protest, but protests must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property.

questions.q: Do men and women have equal rights in Australia?
questions.a: Yes, men and women have equal rights
questions.e: Men and women have equal rights in Australia. It is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender.

questions.q: Under the Rule of Law, who must obey Australia's laws?
questions.a: Everyone, including government, religious and business leaders and the police
questions.e: No person, group or religious rule is above the law. Everyone, including people in positions of power, must obey Australia's laws.

questions.q: If an Australian law and a religious practice conflict, which one must be followed?
questions.e: Where there is a conflict between an Australian law and a religious practice, Australian law prevails. Religious laws have no legal status in Australia.

questions.q: Which of these is a privilege of Australian citizenship?
questions.e: Australian citizens can apply for an Australian passport and re-enter Australia freely.

questions.q: Which of these is a responsibility of Australian citizens?
questions.a: Serving on a jury if called to do so
questions.e: Citizens must obey the law, vote, defend Australia should the need arise, and serve on a jury if called to do so. Service in the Defence Force is voluntary.

questions.q: Who must vote in federal and state or territory elections?
questions.a: Australian citizens aged 18 years or over
questions.e: Voting is a responsibility for Australian citizens aged 18 years or over, and it is compulsory.

questions.q: While overseas, what can Australian citizens ask for in times of need?
questions.a: Consular help from an Australian government official
questions.e: Australian citizens can ask for help from an Australian embassy, high commission or consulate overseas. They must still obey the laws of that country.

questions.q: How do representatives in parliament answer to the people for their decisions?
w: They do not have to answer to anyone
questions.e: In a parliamentary democracy, representatives in parliament must answer to the people, through elections, for the decisions they make.
